questions.prompt: What makes a function a Server Action?

options.text: The "use server" directive on the function or its module, and it being async
Exporting it from a Client Component

questions.explanation: A Server Action is an async function marked "use server" (inline or at the top of a module).

questions.prompt: Which statements about Server Actions are true? Select all that apply.

options.text: They run only on the server and can use secrets/database
A form's action prop can call one, receiving FormData
Their arguments and return values must be serializable
They automatically refresh cached UI with no extra code

questions.explanation: Actions are server-only, callable via <form action>, and must be serializable. You must call revalidatePath/revalidateTag to refresh cached UI.

questions.prompt: Type the exact directive string that marks a Server Action.
questions.explanation: "use server" marks a function or module as containing Server Actions.

questions.prompt: Match each piece to its role in a Server Action.

pairs.right: Sends the user to another page

questions.explanation: The form triggers the action, FormData carries the input, revalidatePath refreshes data, and redirect navigates afterward.

questions.prompt: Order what happens when a form backed by a Server Action is submitted.

items.text: Next.js runs the Server Action on the server with the FormData
The action mutates data and calls revalidatePath
The affected UI re-renders with fresh data

questions.explanation: Submitting runs the action server-side; it mutates and revalidates, so the UI updates with the new data.
